description: LLM Model Status SPA foundation - a standalone Svelte 5 app (apps/solar-status) served by solar-control at /status. Scope: app scaffold, dual serving modes (separate Vite dev server / embedded in solar-control Docker image), backend plumbing (reserved /api/status route returning 501, static serving, CORS), and repo/CI wiring. Page features, payload schema, and data model for the status functionality are intentionally out of scope and specified separately; the base is built so they can be added without structural changes.

userStories.title: Reserve GET /api/status with a 501 placeholder in solar-control
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the /api/status route reserved under /api returning 501 Not Implemented, so the SPA's API contract endpoint exists without solar-control implementing any status model or logic yet.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/status is registered under the /api router (app/routes/management) and returns HTTP 501 Not Implemented with no body schema commitment
make lint-solar-control test-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: Payload schema, aggregation logic, and realtime behavior are deferred feature decisions; this story only reserves the route.

userStories.title: Serve built SPA at /status from solar-control
userStories.description: As an operator, I want solar-control to serve the built SPA at /status when a dist/ is present, so production runs same-origin with solar-control as the only runtime dependency.
acceptanceCriteria: New optional config setting STATUS_DIST_DIR in app/config.py; default resolved relative to the solar-control package pointing at the sibling SPA checkout (apps/solar-status/dist)
APIRouter included with prefix /status registers FastAPI app.frontend(): router.frontend('/', directory=<dist path>, fallback='auto')
Frontend router registered only if the dist directory exists at startup - without a build, /status 404s and control starts/tests fine without Node
check_dir=False is avoided (it would 500 at request time instead of 404ing cleanly)
fallback='auto' serves index.html for client-side-routed navigations while missing assets still 404; no hand-written SPA catch-all
Regular path operations take precedence - /api and /v1 remain safe
Unit tests cover registration with and without an existing dist directory
make lint-solar-control test-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: Uses FastAPI's built-in app.frontend() (available since 0.141.x, which solar-control pins). Docker sets STATUS_DIST_DIR=/app/status-ui explicitly (see US-009).

userStories.title: Add configurable CORS policy to solar-control
userStories.description: As a developer, I want a configurable CORS allow-list on solar-control, so the dev-mode SPA can call the control API cross-origin while production stays unaffected.
acceptanceCriteria: CORS middleware added to solar-control with allow-listed origins from CORS_ORIGINS env var
Default (CORS_ORIGINS unset/empty) means CORS disabled - same-origin production path unaffected
Dev Vite origin can be allow-listed locally via env
Unit tests cover enabled and disabled states
make lint-solar-control test-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: CANCELLED by decision: CORS does not need to be configurable. solar-control keeps its open policy (allow_origins=["*"]) for any origin, exactly as before this story; the configurable CORS_ORIGINS implementation was reverted. The dev-mode SPA can call the API cross-origin with no extra setup. Separate open decision still standing: whether the status page/API is public read-only or gated by an optional key via env (mirroring SOLAR_WEBUI_AUTH_KEY). Foundation ships without a gate.

userStories.title: Scaffold apps/solar-status (Svelte 5 + Vite + TS)
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a new standalone Svelte app in the pnpm workspace, so the status SPA follows the repo's one-app-one-toolchain convention instead of extending solar-webui.
acceptanceCriteria: Svelte 5 + Vite + TypeScript app scaffolded in apps/solar-status
apps/solar-status added to pnpm-workspace.yaml (exact paths)
Conditional Vite base: '/' for the dev server, '/status/' for the production build
Tailwind configured for styling consistency with solar-webui
vitest + @testing-library/svelte set up with at least a smoke test
pnpm --filter solar-status build produces dist/
userStories.notes: No Svelte exists anywhere in the repo today - this is a new toolchain, not a React extension.

userStories.title: Implement mode-agnostic data layer with API base resolution
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a single code path in the SPA that works with both an absolute API base (dev) and a relative one (embedded), so only the injected base URL string differs between serving modes.
acceptanceCriteria: Typed fetch client resolves the API base once at startup: new URL(import.meta.env.VITE_API_BASE ?? '../api', new URL(import.meta.env.BASE_URL, location.origin))
Vite BASE_URL is used as the mount-point anchor so relative resolution is independent of the active client-side route; no <base> tag needed
Endpoint paths are appended to the resolved base (${apiBase}/status pattern)
Dev: absolute VITE_API_BASE ignores the mount anchor; embedded: ../api resolves to same-origin /api at any route depth
Unit tests cover base resolution for both modes
pnpm --filter solar-status test passes
userStories.notes: Browser resolves fetch()/EventSource() against document.baseURI, hence the SPA-side resolution against the mount point.

userStories.title: Dev server serving mode (SPA separately from solar-control)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want to run the SPA on its own Vite dev server alongside solar-control, so I can develop without building the SPA or running it from control.
acceptanceCriteria: Vite dev server runs on its own port (5174) serving the app at '/' - no proxying
.env.development sets VITE_API_BASE=http://localhost:8000
SPA at http://localhost:5174/ calls solar-control directly cross-origin (CORS allow-list must include the dev origin)
solar-control runs without any SPA build in this mode
Verified in browser: make dev-control + make dev-status, open http://localhost:5174/ (dev-browser skill)

userStories.title: Add Makefile targets for solar-status
userStories.description: As a developer, I want standard Makefile targets for the new app, so local workflows and the CI matrix use the same entry points.
acceptanceCriteria: make dev-status starts the Vite dev server
make test-solar-status and make lint-solar-status exist (target names match CI matrix app names)
Targets wired into the aggregate make test and make lint
make lint and make test pass on a clean checkout

userStories.title: Wire solar-status into CI (dispatcher + quality gates)
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want CI to run the new app's gates and to couple solar-control's status API paths with the SPA's tests, so cross-boundary contract changes cannot break the SPA silently.
acceptanceCriteria: ci.yaml dispatcher case for apps/solar-status/* paths + ALL=1 list updated
solar-control's status route/schema paths (app/routes/management status files, app/services/host_status.py) additionally trigger the solar-status gates
quality-gates.yaml gains an install branch for solar-status (pnpm + Node 24, mirroring the solar-webui branch)
CI runs green on a change touching both solar-control status paths and apps/solar-status
userStories.notes: Path-based dispatch alone would not couple the two sides of the /api/status contract.

userStories.title: Embed SPA build into solar-control Docker image
userStories.description: As an operator, I want the built SPA baked into the solar-control image, so a single image serves the API and the status page with no new Docker image for the SPA.
acceptanceCriteria: solar-control Dockerfile gains a Node build stage that runs pnpm --filter solar-status build (repo-root build context for lockfile access, like solar-webui)
dist/ (apps/solar-status/dist/) copied into the runtime image at a fixed path (/app/status-ui)
Dockerfile sets ENV STATUS_DIST_DIR=/app/status-ui so the embedded serving mode activates automatically
.github/release-manifest.json: solar-control entry updated (likely context: '.'); no new component for the SPA
Image size / .dockerignore implications reviewed
Built image serves http://localhost:8000/status
userStories.notes: Docker image name for solar-control stays unchanged (aiops/* names are fixed).

userStories.title: Verify both serving modes end to end
userStories.description: As a developer, I want both serving modes verified against the acceptance path in the plan, so the foundation is proven before feature work starts.
acceptanceCriteria: make lint-solar-status test-solar-status passes
Full make test lint passes
Serving mode 1 (dev): make dev-control + make dev-status, http://localhost:5174/ loads and calls control on the absolute VITE_API_BASE
Serving mode 2 (embedded): build the SPA, run make dev-control alone, http://localhost:8000/status serves the built assets
